Fact checks›Property tax

The claim

A 220 percent property tax increase

“The council raised your property taxes 220 percent.”

Seen: Yard signs, petition sheets and city Facebook groups, June to August 2026.

Our finding Overtaken by events

It was true of a decision that has since been changed or repealed.

220.88% was noticed in June and never adopted. The rate that survives is 0.000900: 69.81% over the certified rate, on the city's own line, which is about a tenth of a property tax bill.

The numbers

Noticed, June+220.88% · never adopted0.001700
Adopted 6 August+183.02% · repealed 12 days later0.001500
In force+69.81% over the certified rate0.000900
Average homewas $314.03 as noticed+$99.31 a year

What’s true

The number was real and the city printed it. The Truth-in-Taxation notice mailed in June proposed 0.001700 against a 0.000530 certified rate and stated the increase as 220.88%: a rise in the city's budgeted property tax revenue over the prior year, excluding eligible new growth.

What changed

Two things. The figure is three rates out of date: the council adopted 0.001500 on August 6, repealed it on August 18, and adopted 0.000900 in its place. And it was never a percentage of anybody's tax bill (it is a percentage of the city's own levy, which is one of seven lines on an Eagle Mountain bill), the fourth-largest of them on today's bill, and the third once the new rate is levied.

More detail

On the notice's own average home ($488,000 of market value, $268,400 taxable after Utah's 55% primary-residence exemption), the noticed rate would have added $314.03 a year. The rate in force adds $99.31.

On that same home the city's line goes from about $143 a year to about $242, inside a total bill of about $2,517 at 2025 rates. That is the city's share moving from roughly 5.7% of the bill to roughly 9.2% of it. Alpine School District's line alone is more than six times the city's.

Still provisional. The 0.000900 is certain; the vote, the motion and the figures the adopting resolution recites were not published when this was written, so everything priced at that rate here is this project's arithmetic on it.
